fields.mechanism: Multi-point attachment system inspired by gecko footpad adhesion technology
fields.intervention: Incorporate microstructured adhesive surfaces on the haptics of intraocular lenses to create multiple attachment points with the eye's anatomy
fields.expected_effect: Enhanced fixation stability through distributed adhesion forces that maintain lens position without relying solely on anatomical structures
fields.falsification_test: In vitro testing comparing dislodgement forces between standard IOLs and gecko-inspired adhesive IOLs under simulated eye movement conditions
fields.mechanism_source_span: (No direct source span in provided paper - this is a cross-industry transfer from biomimetic adhesion technology)

fields.mechanism: Three-haptic angle-supported design for fixation in absence of standard anatomical prerequisites
fields.intervention: Implement a multi-haptic configuration that distributes forces across the anterior chamber angle rather than relying on single-point fixation, reducing mechanical stress at any one point
fields.expected_effect: Decreased mechanical stress on the lens-ocular interface, preventing gradual deformation or displacement that leads to dislocation
fields.falsification_test: Finite element analysis comparing stress distribution between single-haptic and three-haptic designs under simulated eye movement and pressure changes
fields.mechanism_source_span: A custom foldable, three-haptic, angle-supported AC-IOL (VKL Type 37 F, Design Kermani; Morcher GmbH, Stuttgart, Germany)

fields.mechanism: Custom-made foldable, hydrophilic-acrylic, angle-supported anterior chamber intraocular lens with three-haptic design
fields.intervention: Replace standard rigid angle-supported IOL with a custom-designed foldable three-haptic AC-IOL that can be customized to individual anatomical constraints
fields.expected_effect: Improved stability and reduced dislocation risk due to better anatomical matching and enhanced fixation through three-point haptic support
fields.falsification_test: Compare dislocation rates between standard rigid angle-supported IOLs and custom three-haptic AC-IOLs in patients with similar anatomical limitations over a 3-year follow-up period
fields.mechanism_source_span: "We describe the development and three-year clinical outcome of a custom-made, foldable, hydrophilic-acrylic, angle-supported AC-IOL implanted in an eye in which neither sulcus nor iris-claw fixation was feasible."

fields.mechanism: Multi-physics hybrid of mechanical anchoring and hydrodynamic stabilization
fields.intervention: Design intraocular lens with micro-patterned surface that combines mechanical angle-fixation points with hydrophilic properties that create controlled adhesion to aqueous humor
fields.expected_effect: Enhanced stability through both mechanical fixation and fluid dynamics control, reducing dislodgement risk while maintaining biocompatibility
fields.falsification_test: In vitro testing in dynamic eye models with varying aqueous humor flow rates and pressure fluctuations
fields.mechanism_source_span: A custom foldable, three-haptic, angle-supported AC-IOL (VKL Type 37 F, Design Kermani; Morcher GmbH, Stuttgart, Germany)

fields.mechanism: Custom foldable, three-haptic, angle-supported anterior chamber intraocular lens design
fields.intervention: Modify intraocular lens to incorporate a custom foldable, three-haptic, angle-supported design using hydrophilic-acrylic material instead of rigid PMMA
fields.expected_effect: Enhanced stability and fixation in the anterior chamber without relying on capsular support or iris attachment, reducing dislodgement risk
fields.falsification_test: Compare dislodgement rates between custom three-haptic angle-supported AC-IOLs and traditional rigid angle-supported IOLs in eyes with inadequate capsular support and anatomical prerequisites for other fixation methods
